propositions: A model class configured with a canonical versioned Bedrock model id containing a colon (e.g., 'us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0') silently drops the explicit provider='bedrock' setting because the colon in the version suffix is misinterpreted as a provider separator.

The _resolve_target function's test '":
" in model' incorrectly treats the colon in a model id's version suffix as a provider-model separator, returning the unqualified model and discarding the configured provider.

An unqualified versioned Bedrock id is later parsed as 'provider:model' on the first colon, causing infer_provider to extract a garbage fragment (e.g., 'us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1') that cannot be found in the provider registry.
The failure manifests as an error reporting an unknown provider that is actually part of the model id, contradicting the operator's explicit configuration and obscuring the true misconfiguration.
The fix must check an explicitly configured provider first before scanning the model string, ensuring no punctuation in the model id can override or discard an explicit instruction.
